**Status:** Reproduced at 495e1d3 (Go 1.24.4, linux/amd64). The panic showed up in 5 of 5 runs, each within a few seconds.

**Expected:** Calling `Command.Run` on two separate `*cli.Command` values at the same time shouldn't panic.

**Actual:** One subtest panics with `runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference`, the same symptom as the report. Stack trace:
```
(*boolValue).Get                 flag_bool.go:71   (*b.destination, destination is nil)
(*FlagBase).Get                  flag_impl.go:192
(*Command).Value                 command.go:533
(*Command).Bool                  flag_bool.go:28
(*Command).checkHelp             command.go:186
(*Command).run                   command_run.go:198
```

**Trigger:** Two goroutines each call `Run` on their own `cli.Command`, using the default help settings (help not hidden). Every command shares the one global `HelpFlag` (`flag.go:43`). On each `Run`, `ensureHelp` resets that shared flag in place (`command_setup.go:203-209`: `applied=false`, `value=nil`, and so on). If one goroutine resets it while the other is between setting up its flags and `checkHelp`, the second one reads a `boolValue` whose `destination` is nil. Running with `-race` confirms it: there are data-race reports on those writes in `ensureHelp` (`command_setup.go:205`, `:207`).

**Run:** `go test ./repro/issue2176/ -run Test_run -count 100000 -failfast` (for the race reports: `go test -race ./repro/issue2176/ -count 20`)

**Artifacts:** `repro/issue2176/debug_test.go` is the reporter's test as written, with only a stack trace added to the recover message. It sits in its own package so the other tests in the `cli` package can't change `HelpFlag` underneath it.

I didn't change any production code.
